newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn appeals to Yemen to help free German hostages.
newsitem.headline: Bonn appeals to Yemen to help free German hostages.

text.p: The Foreign Ministry said on Thursday it had appealed to Yemen's security services to do all they can to free seven German tourists kidnapped while travelling in southeastern Yemen on motorcycles.
The ministry said Yemen President Ali Abdullah Saleh had met German ambassador Helga Graefin Strachwitz and said he had personally taken on the case, setting up three emergency committees.
The ministry statement came as Yemeni security forces laid siege to southeastern parts of the country to help free the men.
They were seized by gunmen in the Wadi al-Dabaat between Mahra and Hadramaut provinces on Monday.

Official sources said the kidnappers, all local tribesmen, wanted to put pressure on the government to bring to justice an alleged Yemeni swindler who sold them smuggled cars brought in from Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states.
The source said the abductors had telephoned local authorities to ask for 12 million marks ($7 million) ransom.
Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil companies have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners in recent years to use as bargaining chips.
An American diplomat and a Saudi ambassador have been among the kidnap victims. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions and all the hostages have been released unharmed.
Some were rescued by security forces, others were set free.
